whatIs.title: Two directions, one AI voice
whatIs.para1: Inbound-Outbound AI Voice is an AI phone assistant that works both ways. Inbound, it greets your customers, understands what they're calling about, books appointments and passes the important cases on to your team. Outbound, it places the calls itself: confirmations, reminders, follow-ups on quotes, or news of a slot that just opened up.
whatIs.para2: Unlike a receptionist, it never takes time off. It answers on the second ring at 8 in the evening, it takes five calls at once during the morning rush, and it never forgets to call back. Your team stops getting interrupted, and no customer ends up in voicemail.
whatIs.para3: You decide the scope: inbound only, outbound only, or both on the same number.

inbound.title: Inbound
inbound.desc: Answers within seconds, books into your calendar, handles the questions that come up again and again, and transfers to your team when a case needs a human.

outbound.title: Outbound
outbound.desc: Places calls with confirmations, day-before reminders, follow-ups on quotes and rebooking of cancelled slots – in your name and in your words.

example.title: What a real call sounds like
example.subtitle: Two actual conversations – one inbound, one outbound. Word for word as the AI runs them, along with everything it handled along the way.

inbound.situation: 8:41 PM, an hour and a half after closing. Normally this call would hit voicemail – and the customer would move on to the next plumber on the list.

chat.text: You've reached Aibooking at Northside Plumbing. How can I help?
Hi. I've got a pipe dripping under the kitchen sink. Can someone come out?
We can help with that. Is there water on the floor right now, or is it a slow drip?
It's a slow drip. I've put a bucket under it.
Good. Then I'll book a standard visit rather than an emergency call-out – that's cheaper for you. I have tomorrow at 8:30 AM or Thursday at 1 PM.
Perfect. Could I get the address and a mobile number for the confirmation?
Thank you. You're booked for tomorrow at 8:30 AM. You'll get an SMS confirmation now and a reminder an hour before.

inbound.outcomesLabel: What the AI handled along the way
outcomes: Answered in two seconds – an hour and a half after closing
Assessed whether the job was urgent and picked the right job type
Found an open slot in the right engineer's calendar
Logged the address and phone number straight onto the job
Sent the confirmation and scheduled the reminder automatically

outbound.situation: 9:15 AM the day before. The AI calls through tomorrow's appointments itself, so cancellations get caught in good time instead of turning into no-shows.

chat.text: Hi Emma. This is Aibooking calling on behalf of Clinic Sund. I'm calling about your appointment tomorrow at 10 AM – does that still work?
Oh, I'd completely forgotten. I'm actually at work until 3.
That's no problem at all. I can offer tomorrow at 3:45 PM, or Friday at 9:30 AM. Which suits you better?
Your appointment is moved to Friday at 9:30 AM. You'll get an SMS with the new time now. Have a good day.

outbound.outcomesLabel: What the AI handled along the way
outcomes: Called through tomorrow's appointments without anyone having to remember
Caught the cancellation the day before instead of at the no-show
Offered a new slot immediately, while the customer was still on the line
Freed up the 10 AM slot and offered it to the next person on the waiting list
Updated the calendar and sent the new confirmation

faqSubtitle: What we're asked most often before an AI voice goes live.

faq.question: What is the difference between inbound and outbound calls?
faq.answer: Inbound is when the customer calls you – the AI picks up, helps with whatever they're calling about, and books or transfers. Outbound is when the AI places the call itself, typically with reminders, confirmations or follow-ups on a quote. You can use one direction or both on the same number.

faq.question: Can I keep my current phone number?
faq.answer: Yes. You keep your number and we set up forwarding. You decide when the AI takes over: on every call, only outside opening hours, or only when the line is busy or goes unanswered after a set number of rings.

faq.question: How many calls can it handle at once?
faq.answer: There's no upper limit on simultaneous calls. If ten customers call at the same time, all ten are answered immediately. You pay for the talk time actually used, not for capacity, so a busy Monday morning doesn't cost extra in subscription.

faq.question: Can customers tell it's an AI?
faq.answer: The voice is natural, but we always recommend it introduces itself as a digital assistant – it's both the honest approach and the one customers respond best to. You decide the exact wording of the greeting.

faq.question: What happens if the AI can't help?
faq.answer: It's set up to recognise its own limits. For complaints, urgent cases or questions it has no answer to, it transfers to the right colleague, or takes a message with name, number and what the case is about so you can call back.

faq.question: Is automated outbound calling legal?
faq.answer: Yes, when you comply with GDPR and marketing law. Service-related calls to existing customers – reminders, confirmations, rebooking – don't require separate consent. Pure marketing does, and the recipient must always be able to opt out of further calls. The system handles opt-outs for you.

faq.question: Does it work in languages other than English?
faq.answer: Yes. Alongside English the AI handles Danish, German, Spanish, French and Portuguese among others, and it switches language by itself if the customer does. That's particularly useful if you have international customers or staff.

faq.question: What does it cost compared to a receptionist?
faq.answer: A full-time receptionist typically costs EUR 47,000–60,000 a year including pension and holiday pay. The AI voice starts at EUR 200 a month and covers the phone around the clock, through holidays and sick days too.

faq.question: How long does setup take?
faq.answer: Usually under a week. We start with a conversation about your services and workflows, set up the voice and the calendar integration, and you test it free for seven days before deciding.
